The statement is cautious about near-term growth and inflation due to COVID-19, but it is paired with strong accommodation and broad market backstops. Consistent with the FSR, the FOMC held the funds rate at 0–0.25%, continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, and reinforced forward guidance via average-inflation targeting. The FSR notes these actions—along with facilities such as the CPFF, SMCCF, TALF, MLF, the FIMA repo facility, and expanded dollar swap lines—supported credit availability to households, small and medium-sized businesses, financial institutions, and municipalities, helping restore market functioning and keep overall financial conditions accommodative. At the same time, the FSR highlights elevated vulnerabilities: the pandemic continues to weigh on activity and employment, business debt and CRE risks are notable, and delinquencies and defaults could rise, especially among smaller firms and more vulnerable households. Net tone: cautious on the outlook but materially supportive on policy and market functioning.
